(2) One is called puthujjana, because he has a lot of sakkāyadiṭṭhi that is not yet removed (not removed) (because he causes sakkāyadiṭṭhi etc.) (3) One is called puthujjana, because he looks up at the faces of many teachers. (4) One is called puthujjana, because he does not get up from all the gati. (5) One is called puthujjana, because he performs-arranges various abhisaṅkhāra (arranging) natures. (6) One is called puthujjana, because he is carried by various oghas. (7) One is called puthujjana, because he is heated with various natures that cause to be heated (because he is heated by various natures that cause to be heated.) (8) One is called puthujjana, because he is burnt by various natures that cause to be burnt. (9) One is called puthujjana, because he lusts for a lot of five pleasures. (10) One is called puthujjana, because he is hindered by a lot of five nīvaraṇas. (11) One is called puthujjana, because he is included in those who practice many evil deeds. (12) One is called puthujjana, because he is separated from the noble ones. He is various as kalyāṇaputhujjana, andhaputhujjana etc. In Thomanidhi, the following meanings also are there, one who is inferior, one who lacks wisdom, one who is cruel.

puthuvī:
[Putha+ī]  CL=8 The word 'pathavī' (earth) has several synonyms in Dhātu 181:
- Vasundharā
- Chamā
- Bhūmi
- Medinī
- Mahī
Grammatical Formation:
1. From root 'puthu' + 'ī'
2. Can become:
- puthavī
- pathavī
- paṭhavī
The word has five main meanings:
1. Physical Earth (sasambhāra pathavī):
- The ground/earth mixed with color, smell, etc.
2. Earth Element (pathavī dhātu):
- The quality of hardness and solidity
- One of the four primary elements
3. Earth Kasiṇa:
- Meditation object/device
- Visual representation of earth element
4. Earth Deity:
- Beings associated with earth element
5. Conceptual Term:
- The name/concept 'pathavī' itself
The etymology comes from 'patthaṭa' meaning 'spread out' or 'extended,' as earth is spread out everywhere. This is explained in various texts including the Visuddhimagga (1.360) and its commentary.
puthuvīputhavīpathavī: [ puthapuda + itthī ī. Puthapuda + ṇa. Pa + thava dhāta + a. Itthī ī paccaññaḥ. Pa + thara + a. Itthī ī paccaññaḥ. (dhāna,ṭī.) puthu-puda + ī. (kaccaññaḥ.) putha- dhāta + kvi, īpaccaññaḥ. (rū.) puthupuda + vī. (moga,3.) pāṭipadikapuda. (ma,ṭī,1.) puthaiti pāṭipadike ṭhite nadādi ī, puthassa puthuādese vuddhimhi ca kateputhavī, ussuvādese puthuvī. Pathādese pathathī. Imaspiṃ pakkhe avādeso. Atha vā thava gatiyaṃ, pathavati etthāti pathavī, nadādi. Sabbattha pattharatīti vā pathavī, thara santharaṇe, papubbo, rassa vo, nadādi, puthavī, assu. Dhāna, ṭī. 181. Puthu hutvā jātanti puthavī,... Pathavī, paṭhavī vā. Kaccaññaḥ. 666. Putha-vitthāre, patthaṭātiatthe kvipaccayo. Rū, nhā. 417. Vīmhi puthussa pathava puthavā honti. Moga, 3. 39. Puthulaṭṭhena puthuvī, puthuvī eva pathavī. Ma,ṭī, 1. 67. ] (thī) CL=10 The Earth.

The millionaire Anāthapiṇḍika went to the palace wearing a ring and good clothes and some drunkards called him to the wine cellar, praised the wine saying it was good and asked him to drink. He noticed that the wine bowl was full even though they were praising it was good. Then he knew that the drunkards have mixed sleeping pills in the wine and their plan was to steal the ring and the cloths after he lose his consciousness. Then he chased them away. Jā, 1.13. puttamasūpamasuttanta: [ puttamaṃsūpama + suttanta ] (pu,na) CL=10 The discourse which has-which is preached using eating the flesh of child as the simile.
puttamasūpamovāda: [ puttamaṃsūupama + ovāda ] (pu) CL=10 The speech of admonishing-admonishment which uses eating the flesh of child as the simile.
puttasakilesa: [ putta + saṃkilesa ] (pu) CL=10 The mental heat-impurity that appears upon-because of the child.
puñchitu: [ puñcha(puchi) + tuṃ ] (kri,vi) CL=7 To wipe off.
puñjitu: ___ In Pācit, Yo, 471, there is the word 'Puñjitunti sodhetuṃ'. Puñjituṃ -must be there.
puññasakā: [ puñña + saṃkāsa(saṅkāsa) ] (saṅkā)sa (ti) CL=10 Similar to merit.
puññābhinisasa: [ puñña + abhinisaṃsa ] (pu) CL=10 The profit-consequence of merit.
puññūpasahita: [ puñña + upasaṃhita ] (ti) CL=10 That which relies on-related merit, One who gives merit.
puṇṇakasa: [ puṇṇa + kaṃsa ] (pu) CL=10 A golden cup filled with gold.
puṭasa: [ puṭa + aṃsa ] (ti) CL=10 One who has a bag (of provisions for a journey that is hung) in the shoulder, One who has hung a bag of provisions for a journey. See-puṭosa.
